newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/WorldCom, Zitel remain busy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/WorldCom, Zitel remain busy.

text.p: The final trading day in 1996 for individual equity options was relatively quiet, with some recently common names still garnering most of the action.
On the Pacific Stock Exchange, options on shares of WorldCom Inc saw fairly heavy action, mostly on the call side as the stock rallied.
The WorldCom January 25 call traded more than 4,200 contracts making it most active in the group. The January 30 call traded about 3,370 and the January 27-1/2 call traded more than 2,800.
Among WorldCom puts, the January 25 traded about 1,080 contracts, making it by far the most active put.
WorldCom shares gained 1-5/16 to 26-1/16 on a heavy 30.15 million shares. The company said its $12.6 billion stock swap merger with MFS Communications Co Inc Inc was completed.
WorldCom calls have been very active in the last couple of weeks as speculation grew that the company would be bought by another telecommunications firm, traders said.
After being stuck in the low 20's despite the heavy call activity, the shares began to move higher last week.
In other activity, volatility remained high and trading volumes strong in options on shares of Zitel Corp as the stock saw another volatile day.
Zitel shares, which rose to an all-time high of 72-7/8 before slumping more than 20 points to close at 41 on Monday, rebounded 3-3/8 to 44-3/8. The stock bounced between a low of 35 and a high of 48.
"If you weren't doing Zitel, you weren't doing much," one options trader in Chicago said.
Among the Zitel options, the January 50, 55 and 60 calls saw heavy order flow, as did the January 35, 40 and 45 puts.
The trader said that after Monday's action, the stock would take some time to recover.
